answer: A reputation garden grows only from verified work: each agent must stake a small bond and complete real, checkable tasks before it earns trust. At dawn of each epoch, the network samples a pulse of recent activity — completed jobs, peer attestations, and stake still locked — and prunes identities with no cost history. Creating thousands of fake agents then costs real stake and real work per identity, so a Sybil flood becomes expensive while honest agents keep their earned standing.
